exercises.title: The traps disappear
exercises.body: Here is the reward for everything so far. English makes you agonise over its and it’s, their and there — pairs that sound identical and are spelled apart. Shavian spells sound, so they are simply the same word: it’s and its are both 𐑦𐑑𐑕; their and there are both 𐑞𐑺. You will never have to choose again.

exercises.title: More pairs that collapse
exercises.body: It keeps happening. Son and sun are both 𐑕𐑳𐑯; sea and see are both 𐑕𐑰; whole and hole are both 𐑣𐑴𐑤; new and knew are both 𐑯𐑿. English keeps a silent letter around to tell each pair apart on the page — Shavian lets the sentence do that job, exactly as speech has always done.

exercises.title: But listen properly
exercises.body: Not every English look-alike is a homophone. Say your and you’re slowly: 𐑘𐑹 and 𐑿𐑼 really are different sounds, and Shavian keeps them apart. Same for their 𐑞𐑺 and they’re 𐑞𐑱𐑼. The rule never changes — write what you hear — but that means hearing carefully.
